title: Shifting a Fractional-Power Curve Right and Down
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: The graph of y = x^(2/3) is to be shifted right 1 unit and down 1 unit. Give an equation for the shifted graph and describe the original and shifted curves.

steps.title: Apply the Horizontal Shift (Right 1 Unit)
steps.explanation: Replace x with x - 1 in y = x^(2/3) to shift the graph 1 unit to the right.
steps.why: Horizontal translation to the right by 1 unit replaces x with x - 1.

steps.title: Apply the Vertical Shift (Down 1 Unit)
steps.explanation: Subtract 1 from the expression (or replace y with y + 1) to shift the curve 1 unit downward.
steps.why: Vertical translation downward by 1 unit subtracts 1 from the function output.

steps.title: Identify Key Graphical Landmarks
steps.explanation: The parent curve y = x^(2/3) is symmetric about the y-axis with a sharp cusp at (0, 0). The shifted curve y = (x - 1)^(2/3) - 1 has its cusp at (1, -1), is symmetric about x = 1, and crosses the x-axis at (0, 0) and (2, 0).
steps.why: Translating by (1, -1) moves the cusp from (0, 0) to (1, -1) and the axis of symmetry from x = 0 to x = 1.
